subject.title: LaunchAgent generator discards stderr (/dev/null), and the 2026.7.1 fail-closed migration gate deadlocks on a stale legacy plugin index that doctor --fix cannot repair

question: Should generated macOS LaunchAgents use a managed local stderr log path and preserve explicit operator redirects across regeneration, or should service output be controlled only through an explicit OpenClaw configuration surface?
rationale: Both a default log location and retention of hand-edited plist fields are user-visible service-management contracts; choosing one affects upgrades, supportability, and launchd failure modes.

options.title: Managed local log with explicit override preservation
options.body: Default stderr to an OpenClaw-controlled path under the user’s local Library logs directory and retain an existing non-default redirect unless regeneration is explicitly forced.

options.title: Managed output only
options.body: Always regenerate a canonical local stderr path and provide a documented OpenClaw configuration or command for operators who need a different destination.

options.title: Keep stderr suppressed
options.body: Retain `/dev/null` and rely on another structured diagnostic path, only if that path demonstrably captures startup failures before launchd restarts.

recommendation.title: Managed local log with explicit override preservation
recommendation.body: Default stderr to an OpenClaw-controlled path under the user’s local Library logs directory and retain an existing non-default redirect unless regeneration is explicitly forced.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent startup-migration and readiness-gate work makes this the closest evidence-backed routing candidate for the coupled recovery behavior.
